text:
Maya: heads-up: nightly eval flagged a big hit-rate slump for rag_promptset_longtail — failure rate 6.2% (was 0.8% yesterday) at 03:00 UTC. Anyone touched reranker/embeddings pipeline yesterday?
EvalBot: automated alert — test=rag_promptset_longtail, metric=hit_rate@topk10, baseline=0.992 -> current=0.938, delta=-0.054. Full CSV: s3://redwood-evals/nightlies/1767771234/metrics.csv
Oliver: I did a canary deploy of quantized-reranker-v2 around 22:30 UTC (PR #4537). It only affected CPU fallback path, but could change scoring. cc @Sophie for embeddings.
Sophie: looking now. Quick check: average anchor->candidate cosine dropped ~0.12 vs baseline on sampled queries (long-tail). Possible embed drift from last refresh. Ran: `python eval/compare_embeddings.py --baseline s3://vecs/nightly/1767600000 --current s3://vecs/nightly/1767700000 --sample-size 5k` -> output: mean_cosine_baseline=0.812, mean_cosine_current=0.692
Amanda: important: we also rolled the index merge that prunes low-usage shards yesterday morning. Could reduce recall for tail docs. Index commit 2026-03-18T08:14Z.
Raj: KV-cache prefill doesn't touch retriever outputs, so unlikely culprit. But reranker scoring changes + index prune is a plausible combo.
Maya: prioritized triage plan: 1) revert quant-reranker canary -> canary-only revert to isolate. 2) re-run embed similarity histograms and per-cohort recall. 3) sample 50 failing prompts and look at generated context + bad generations. Assign: @Oliver revert canary, @Sophie run embed diagnostics, I'll pull samples and run quick manual evals.
Oliver: reverting now — `deploy rollback --service reranker --tag quantized-v2-canary` -> started. ETA ~7m. Will post deploy job id.
Sophie: re-running diagnostics with cohort splits (long-tail, short, multi-hop). Command: ```bash
python eval/embed_drift.py --cohorts longtail,short,multihop --out s3://redwood-evals/1767771234/embed-diagnostics.json
```  Kickoff 03:18 UTC.
Maya: grabbing 50 failed examples from nightlies (ids -> s3://redwood-evals/1767771234/failed_ids.txt) and sampling 10 for manual inspection. Preliminary: many failures are long queries with quoted code blocks that seem to confuse retriever.
Amanda: if revert stabilizes hit-rate, we should also consider temporarily disabling index prune on low-usage shards until we validate.
Raj: also flagging that quantized reranker had slightly different tie-breaking order in PR tests; could change topk ordering when scores are close. Small ranking flips + index prune = drop-through.
Oliver: rollback finished (job 78921). Rolling canary traffic back to baseline. Monitoring logs for reranker scores now.
EvalBot: health-check -> hit_rate@topk10 (post-rollback snapshot): 0.947 (partial recovery). Will re-run full nightly after diagnostics complete.
Sophie: initial embed histograms uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/1767771234/embed-diagnostics.json — longtail cohort shows heavy left-shift in cos sim and higher variance. Attaching top 5 worst-hit doc ids in the file.
Maya: good work. Next steps: Sophie to produce a short PR describing embed delta and suggested refresh cadence. Oliver to revert quant change in prod if rollback stabilizes after one full hourly snapshot. Amanda to delay index prune for 24h. I'll collect sample failure pairs and open a postmortem if nightly stays degraded after full run.
Oliver: noted. If we do full revert, I'll include a tiny test in CI that compares reranker tie-breaking distribution pre/post.
Sophie: one more hypothesis — quantized reranker could amplify small embedding shifts because it compresses score space. I'll run a synthetic rerank test: `python tests/synthetic_rerank.py --embed-perturb 0.05 --quant True/False` and post results.
Maya: thanks all. Please drop quick updates here. :thumbsup:
Oliver: update 03:55 UTC — post-rollback hourly snapshot looks stable at 0.989 for a 1h window. Waiting for full eval.
EvalBot: full-nightly re-run scheduled. Will post final metrics when complete.
